column3: It completes the same detained exchange: the weakened identify the arrogant leaders' continuing inducement to disbelief, then both face the consequence.
It presents disbelief in the Hereafter with deeds made attractive and resulting bewilderment, a secondary account of the condition behind the focus scene.
The return of all matters to God broadly supports the focus's being stopped before the Lord, without its dialogic hierarchy.
It directly stages arrogant leaders addressing the weakened while the latter affirm belief, closely paralleling the focus's unequal exchange.
The nearby denial of the Hour supplies the local disbelief-and-accountability setting that the focus makes visible.
Its refusal to believe after recitation gives only a limited counterpart to the focus's rejection of the Quran.
The immediate reply of the arrogant leaders contests the accusation of obstruction, making the focus's returned speech an actual two-sided dispute.
Its universal mission and warning do not add to the focus's rejection, detention, or reciprocal blame.
Return to the Lord supplies the eschatological destination of the focus's stopped wrongdoers.
It joins false speech, arrogance, and a scene in which wrongdoers confront punishment at death, a related accountability setting.
Criminals being in error and burning gives a general consequence but not the focus's relational structure.
The return of matters to God is a broad eschatological counterpart only.
Criminals stand humbled before their Lord and ask to be returned for faithful action, closely illuminating the focus's stopped scene.
This nearby ayah explicitly names disbelief in the Hereafter, part of the surrounding denial that culminates in the focus's confrontation.
It names the Quran as a clear book, providing a direct counterpoint to the focus's refusal of the Quran.
The weak address the arrogant in the Fire about their former following and inability to bear punishment, a close later form of the focus's accusation.
Its David scene does not clarify the focus's rejection or returned blame.
The Quran's being made easy for remembrance gives a limited counterpoint to refusing it.
Wrongdoers are stopped before their Lord and compelled to acknowledge truth, directly paralleling the focus's judicial tableau.
Social elites call a messenger weak and dismiss his speech, a partial social-power counterpart without the focus's reciprocal blame.
The knowledge of what is before and behind them does not materially develop the focus scene.
Even collective mutual support cannot produce the like of the Quran, reinforcing the distinctive object rejected in the focus.
The nearby claim of wealth, children, and immunity shows the self-assured posture of the deniers in this local sequence.
The command to stop them for questioning sharply clarifies the focus's image of wrongdoers being held.
It records disbelievers' objection to the Quran's mode of descent while affirming its ordered recitation, a focused counterpoint to rejection of it.
Its distinction between personal error and guidance by revelation is only a limited local counterpart.
The rejected secondary reading does not positively clarify the focus relation.
The arrogant explicitly reject what the other party has believed, concisely matching the focus's belief divide.
Disbelievers hear recited signs, respond with arrogance, and are named criminals, a close accountability counterpart.
Demanding the date of the decisive judgment adds little beyond the focus's already-present judgment scene.
Those stopped at the Fire wish to return and become believers, strongly paralleling the focus's stopped deniers and faith question.
Divine knowledge of all movement is only an indirect local setting for the Lord before whom they stand.
Ability to restore is a broad resurrection parallel without the focus's speech or hierarchy.
It contrasts growing belief with doubt and unbelieving questions about a divine sign, a useful parallel to divergent responses to revelation.
Praise of God alone does not add to the focus's concrete relation.
God's encompassing knowledge and human lack of comprehension support the asymmetry of the focus's final confrontation.
Private groups return speech to one another while anticipating argument before their Lord, a notable dialogue-and-accountability parallel.
God's true majesty provides only a broad counterpoint to the arrogant's self-exaltation.
The returning sky does not clarify the focus relation.
Repeated examples in the Quran meet a fixed denial that calls the messengers false, closely paralleling rejection of revealed speech.
The demand to bring back ancestors is a distant resurrection challenge.
Its warning against fabricated speech provides only a limited boundary around the focus's denial of the Quran.
A wrongdoer regrets not taking the messenger's path, a consequential counterpart to blaming others for failed belief.
Turning away arrogantly when verses are recited directly parallels the focus's rejection of the Quran.
Its legal discussion of believing women does not add to the focus's hierarchy or final dispute.
Deniers condition belief on receiving prophetic status themselves, exposing arrogant refusal of the received sign.
It concerns genuinely powerless people without a route, only lexically adjacent to the focus's socially weakened speakers.
The rejected secondary reading does not positively clarify the focus relation.
Its fear of fighting and worldly delay does not develop the focus's relation.
Gratitude and disbelief's consequence do not add a focused connection after earlier stronger candidates.
Return to God in affliction is only a general counterpart to the focus's return before Him.
Selective belief that separates God's messengers supplies a strong counterpart to refusing the Quran and what preceded it.
Adornment of deeds and obstruction from the path gives a secondary account of misdirected agency behind unbelief.
Arrogance is tied to thinking there will be no return to God, directly opposing the focus's enforced return.
The Quran confirms what was before it and cannot be fabricated, directly answering the focus's rejection of both.
All appear before God as the weak ask arrogant leaders whether they can bear punishment, a close parallel with an added answer of helplessness.
Return to the Lord gives the focus's ultimate setting in concise form.
The promised elevation of the oppressed differs from the focus's accountability dialogue among the socially weak.
Divine inheritance and universal return are broad final-account parallels only.
It treats speech between people as a site of satanic provocation, usefully framing the focus's destructive returned words.
Mutual transmission of adorned false speech shows a corrupt speech network, a secondary counterpart to the focus's blame cycle.
Its marriage scene does not clarify the focus relation.
God's possession of what is before and behind does not materially develop the focus.
Believers recognize a divine sign while disbelievers ask what it means, closely paralleling divergent responses to revelation.
The general punishment of opposition does not add to the focus after more direct accountability scenes.
Guarding a messenger before and behind is only a remote counterpart to the focus's phraseology.
Returning to themselves and admitting wrongdoing offers a limited self-accusation parallel.
Its battlefield warning and return threat do not clarify the focus's relation.
The false object cannot return speech or control harm, a limited contrast to accountable reciprocal speech.
Wrongdoers secretly characterize the messenger as bewitched while listening, a concrete example of dismissive speech about revelation.
Those who say they hear while not truly hearing give a concise counterpart to refusing received revelation.
Worship of the Creator is joined to return to Him, opposing the focus's refusal before that return.
Deferring correction until Moses returns is only a distant temporal counterpart to the focus's blame exchange.
Replacement of peoples does not add to the focus's specific relation.
The Quran is taught, providing a direct positive counterpart to the focus's refusal of it.
They claim belief in what was sent to them while rejecting what follows though it confirms what they have, closely paralleling the focus's split rejection.
Human creation does not clarify the focus relation.
Its alliance instruction does not add to the focus's final dialogue.
Wrongdoers fear what they earned while believers receive favor with their Lord, a useful consequence contrast.
Its allocation to alleged partners does not clarify the focus relation.
Seeking refuge when reading the Quran gives only a limited counterpart to the focus's rejection of it.
Excuses are rejected before return to the Knower of unseen and seen, a close accountability-and-disclosure parallel.
The cloud and lightning scene does not clarify the focus relation.
The command to heed what lies before and behind is only a distant phrase-level parallel.
Wrongdoers form a mutually protective network that cannot avail before God, clarifying the limits of collective allegiance.
The drinking-vessel scene does not clarify the focus relation.
Inability to go forward or return is only a distant physical counterpart to the focus's being held.
False partners lack evidence while wrongdoers promise one another delusion, a useful parallel to mutually sustaining false claims.
Its instruction concerning peace does not clarify the focus relation.
God's judgment and return are general eschatological support already supplied more directly above.
When fulfillment comes, former deniers acknowledge the messengers' truth and seek impossible return or intercession, closely extending the focus's scene.
Social ranking becomes a test of recognizing divine favor, a limited counterpart to the focus's weak and arrogant parties.
The sign to Thamud does not add to the focus relation.
Reflection on the Quran is opposed to locked hearts, directly countering the focus's refusal of it.
The contrast between perishing and abiding things does not add to the focus relation.
Communities see their deeds adorned, then return to their Lord to be told what they did, a strong secondary accountability parallel.
Its prayer against deviating hearts does not add a focused connection.
Disbelievers return to God and are informed of their deeds and inward realities, closely supporting the focus's final disclosure.
The absence of a protector or helper is a limited counterpart to leaders' inability to avert the final consequence.
Its ordering of kinship rights does not clarify the focus relation.
It immediately sets an appointed day from which the deniers cannot delay or advance, supplying the temporal frame for the focus's detention.
It generalizes the local pattern: affluent leaders answer every warner with rejection, clarifying the social authority behind the focus's arrogant party.
It corrects the nearby claim that abundance signals exemption, exposing the false confidence that sustains the deniers' stance.
It denies that wealth and children bring people near to God, directly limiting the status logic voiced in the surrounding passage.
Those followed disown their followers when punishment is seen and all ties are cut, a close counterpart to the focus's final blame exchange.
Followers wish for a return so they could disown their leaders, extending the focus's accusation into explicit repudiation and regret.
The arrogant chiefs threaten the messenger and believers with expulsion or forced return, showing coercive elite pressure before the focus's retrospective blame.
Satan denies coercive authority and says he merely called while they answered, sharply qualifying the focus's charge against those who led others astray.
Misleaders bear their own burdens and part of the burdens of those misled, providing an accountability framework for delegated blame.
Those who invoked alleged partners find that they do not answer or provide rescue, a useful boundary on the help the focus's leaders can offer.
The wrongdoer says a close companion led him away from the Reminder, closely paralleling the focus's claim that another party prevented belief.
Mutual affection through false associates turns into denial and cursing on the Day of Resurrection, a close relational counterpart to the focus scene.
Those in the Fire regret not obeying God and the messenger, making the focus's lost belief visible as final remorse.
They explicitly blame their leaders and great ones for leading them astray, an especially close parallel to the focus's weakened speakers.
The condemned approach one another questioning, directly echoing the focus's returned speech among those stopped for judgment.
Followers accuse the other party of approaching them from a position of influence, closely developing the focus's claim of obstruction.
The accused answer that the others were not believers, matching the focus passage's dispute over agency and responsibility.
The leaders deny having authority over the followers and identify their own transgression, a precise counterpart to the next local reply in 34:32.
The misleaders acknowledge leading others astray because they themselves were astray, completing the responsibility pattern raised in the focus.
Both parties share punishment, directly confirming that the focus's reciprocal blame does not remove either side's accountability.
The prophet and the disputants contend before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, closely matching the focus's Lord-centered confrontation.
Calling God false and rejecting truth when it arrives provides a direct characterization of the focus's deniers.
The arrogant answer that all are in the Fire and cannot alter God's judgment, completing the close 40:47 parallel with leaders' acknowledged impotence.
Deniers treat the promise of God and the Hour as mere conjecture, directly supplying the disbelief that the focus brings before judgment.
A companion rejects responsibility for another's transgression before God, a compact parallel to the focus's contested blame.
God prohibits disputing before Him after prior warning, directly framing the focus's exchange as a final, non-exculpatory dispute.
The keepers ask whether a warner came, and the condemned acknowledge rejecting him as mistaken, a focused revelation-and-accountability parallel.
The condemned admit that hearing or reasoning would have kept them from the Fire, deepening the focus's rejected-message theme.
A denier characterizes the revealed message as magic, providing a concrete form of the focus's rejection of the Quran.
Calling the revelation merely human speech gives a direct counter-description of the Quran rejected in the focus.
